title: Discrete worker castes arose by selection eliminating intermediate forms

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Discrete worker castes arose by selection eliminating intermediate forms

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Distinct castes of sterile workers in one nest arose when a graduated series of workers was first formed and then selection on the fertile parents favoured production of the most useful extreme forms until intermediates were no longer produced.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: a graduated series having been first formed, as in the case of the driver ant, and then the extreme forms, from being the most useful to the community, having been produced in greater and greater numbers through the natural selection of the parents which generated them; until none with an intermediate structure were produced.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter VII, “Instinct”; section “Neuter or sterile insects”. Scope: ants with polymorphic worker castes

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch07-14: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.58

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Morphological transitions can be tested comparatively in sampled ants. Existing data are weaker for the asserted selective advantage and exact elimination process.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Map continuous and discrete worker polymorphisms on ant phylogenies and model whether discrete castes derive from graded ancestors, while testing colony performance of extremes versus intermediates. The predicted transition and fitness pattern support the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Historical loss of intermediates is reconstructed rather than observed.

Colony performance data are not centralized.

fields.value:

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The predicted order, graded series first and discrete extremes later, can be examined for ants with public specimens and a tree. That is a partial historical test. The selective elimination step is not in the morphometrics, and missing natural-history data keep the sample well short of all polymorphic ants. Harmonizing caste scores would take months.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Code worker polymorphism as continuous, broadly graded, or discrete without intermediates, and reconstruct the sequence on an ant tree. Discrete castes derived from graded ancestors, as in driver ants relative to their relatives, would support the sequence; discrete castes arising without a graded precursor would count against it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Colony series and caste codes are missing for most species.

Eliminating intermediates by selection is not distinguishable from a developmental switch using shape data alone.

Driver ants are one clade; the scope is polymorphic ants generally.
